overview: Jaxartosaurus (meaning 'Jaxartes River lizard') was a herbivorous lambeosaurine hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Kazakhstan and China, living approximately 90–84 million years ago. Known only from a skull roof and braincase, it is one of the more fragmentarily represented hadrosaurs from Central Asia. Its estimated length of around 9 metres is based on comparisons with related lambeosaurines. It was named by Anatoly Nikolaevich Riabinin in 1939 from material found in the Dabrazhin Formation (Coniacian) of Kazakhstan.

Jaxartosaurus is placed within Lambeosaurinae, the hollow-crested hadrosaurs, suggesting it may have borne a crest similar to those of Parasaurolophus or Corythosaurus. However, the limited material makes the precise crest morphology unknown. Its Central Asian location is significant for understanding hadrosaur biogeography: as hadrosaurs diversified across Laurasia in the Late Cretaceous, Central Asian forms like Jaxartosaurus may represent early members of lineages that later dispersed into both Asia and North America.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: Jaxartosaurus aralensis was described in 1939 by A.N. Riabinin from skull material found in Kazakhstan. The genus name refers to the Jaxartes River (modern Syr Darya), near which the fossils were found, and the species name references the Aral Sea region. Additional material has been tentatively referred to Jaxartosaurus from Xinjiang, China.

articles.title: Known Anatomy and Reconstruction
articles.body: Only a skull roof and braincase are known for Jaxartosaurus, making detailed anatomical reconstruction impossible. The elements present indicate a large hadrosaur and are consistent with lambeosaurine affinities, potentially suggesting a cranial crest, though its form remains unknown. Body size estimates of around 9 metres are extrapolated from related taxa.

articles.title: Palaeoenvironment
articles.body: The Coniacian deposits of Kazakhstan record Late Cretaceous terrestrial environments on the western margins of the Asian continent. Jaxartosaurus would have inhabited river systems and floodplains in this region, in an ecosystem that likely included other ornithopods, ankylosaurs, and theropods of Late Cretaceous Asia.

articles.title: Scientific Significance
articles.body: Jaxartosaurus is one of the few lambeosaurine hadrosaurs documented from Central Asia, and its geographic position is informative for understanding hadrosaur dispersal routes between Asia and North America during the Late Cretaceous. Despite its fragmentary nature, it remains a biogeographically important taxon in studies of Cretaceous hadrosaur diversity.

record.description: Jaxartosaurus aralensis was a hadrosaurid from dinosaur-bearing beds near Kyrk-Kuduk and Alym-Tau in southern Kazakhstan. Its type material is chiefly an incomplete skull; fragmentary postcranial bones from the same deposit have also been referred, but no complete skeleton is known.
facts: The skull is incomplete and the same-deposit postcranium is fragmentary.
The shape of a complete crest cannot be recovered confidently from the preserved type alone.
Herbivory is secure at the hadrosaurid level, but detailed ecology is unknown.

review.ageReviewNote: Rozhdestvensky placed the southern Kazakhstan dinosaur beds containing Jaxartosaurus in the Coniacian-Santonian; the unrelated Syuk-Syuk occurrence is excluded.
